commentary_segments.text: Whether the noise of the cascode plays a role really depends on the load seen by that cascode. In this example the cascode sees the input of a current mirror, which is a low resistor (usually 1/g ). In this case, the m current noise of the cascode can flow from the supply through the diode to ground. It is now added to the output current and to the noise current of the diode. If the cascode were loaded with a very high impedance, in order to create a lot of gain, as is common in opamps, then the noise current of the cascode would be negligible. It is difficult to create a high impedance at the output of the cascode however in this kind of circuit, as it is to work at real high frequencies. The noise current of the cascode will usually be the dominant noise source!
